## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #99571.

Fixes an issue where iOS users scanning a gateway pairing QR could have the scanner dismiss at the wrong time, lose the trust/approval handoff, or crash while VisionKit was still stopping camera capture.

The affected surfaces are the iOS onboarding scanner, Gateway Settings scanner, app/open-url setup-link handling, and post-scan gateway approval handoff.

The scanner now stops VisionKit scanning, queues one typed QR/setup result, dismisses the scanner sheet, and processes pairing only from the sheet dismissal path after a short main-actor settling delay. target.title: fix(gateway-protocol): accept Paperclip adapter metadata in AgentParamsSchema
target.body:
Closes #99458

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where agents dispatched through the Paperclip `openclaw_gateway` adapter fail on every heartbeat run because the gateway's `AgentParamsSchema` rejects the root-level `paperclip` metadata field that the adapter injects. The schema used `{ additionalProperties: false }` without declaring `paperclip`, so valid heartbeat payloads were refused with `invalid agent params: at root: unexpected property 'paperclip'`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added `paperclip: Type.Optional(Type.Unknown())` to `AgentParamsSchema` in `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/agent.ts`. This is the minimal additive fix: the field is tolerated at the gateway boundary without affecting runtime routing, while all other unknown top-level properties are still rejected. A regression test verifies both that the Paperclip payload passes and that unrelated unknown fields still fail validation.

## User Impact

Users and operators running Paperclip-orchestrated agents through the OpenClaw gateway will see heartbeat dispatches succeed instead of failing silently and stalling queued tasks. No changes are required for non-Paperclip callers.

## Evidence

target.title: fix: reject unsupported custom tool_choice in OpenAI Responses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When using the OpenAI provider with the Responses API, tool calls fail with error "Invalid value: 'custom'" because the `reconcileOpenAIResponsesToolChoice` function did not validate or reject `tool_choice` objects with `type: "custom"`.

The OpenAI Responses API does not support `{ type: "custom" }` tool choices. However, the OpenAI SDK types include this option, and without validation, such values were passed directly to the API, causing runtime errors.

**Issue**: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/99856

## Why This Change Was Made

The `reconcileOpenAICompletionsToolChoice` function already handled this case by throwing an error for `custom` types (lines 238-242). However, the corresponding `reconcileOpenAIResponsesToolChoice` function was missing this check, allowing invalid `{ type: "custom" }` values to reach the OpenAI Responses API.

This fix aligns the two functions and prevents invalid `tool_choice` values from causing API errors.

**Changes**:

1. **[src/agents/openai-tool-projection.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/src/agents/openai-tool-projection.ts)**
   - Created internal type `OpenAIResponsesSdkToolChoice` for the full SDK type (line 31)
   - Created exported type `OpenAIResponsesToolChoice` that excludes `{ type: "custom" }` (lines 36-39)
   - Changed `reconcileOpenAIResponsesToolChoice` parameter type to `OpenAIResponsesSdkToolChoice` (line 158)
   - Added runtime check in `reconcileOpenAIResponsesToolChoice` to throw error for `custom` types (lines 176-180)

2. **[src/agents/openai-transport-stream.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/src/agents/openai-transport-stream.ts)**
   - Imported new `OpenAIResponsesToolChoice` type (line 86)
   - Updated `OpenAIResponsesOptions.toolChoice` to use the narrower exported type (line 216)

3. **[src/agents/openai-tool-projection.test.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/src/agents/openai-tool-projection.test.ts)**
   - Added test case to verify `custom` type is correctly rejected by `reconcileOpenAIResponsesToolChoice` (lines 284-290)

## User Impact

- **Before**: Users passing `tool_choice: { type: "custom", name: "xxx" }` would receive cryptic "Invalid value: 'custom'" errors from OpenAI API
- **After**: Users receive a clear error message: "OpenAI Responses custom tool_choice is unsupported because this adapter emits function tools only"

Other valid `tool_choice` types (`"auto"`, `"required"`, `"none"`, `{ type: "function", name: "xxx" }`, `{ type: "allowed_tools", ... }`, and built-in tools like `web_search_preview`) continue to work as expected.

## Evidence

- ✅ `pnpm test src/agents/openai-tool-projection.test.ts` — 15 tests passed
- ✅ `pnpm test src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts` — 286 tests passed
- ✅ `pnpm test src/llm/providers/openai-completions.test.ts` — 37 tests passed
- ✅ `pnpm test src/llm/providers/openai-responses-shared.test.ts` — 34 tests passed
- ✅ `pnpm test src/gateway/openresponses-http.test.ts` — 93 tests passed

**Commit**: `43e489ed5b`  
**Created from**: `openclaw/openclaw@bd2740fedc` (latest main)

target.title: fix(exec): require approval for OpenClaw lifecycle commands
target.body:
Fixes #99518

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where exec commands through gateway or node hosts could let OpenClaw gateway/daemon lifecycle mutations pass through normal allowlist or auto-review paths when they should require explicit approval.

The affected workflow is OpenClaw self-management from exec surfaces: stopping, starting, restarting, running, deleting, or uninstalling the gateway/daemon through CLI, launchctl, systemctl, schtasks, process-kill, shell-wrapper, package-manager, Windows shim, `env -S`, `xargs`/`find`, `sudo`/`doas`, and dispatch-wrapper commands.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a focused lifecycle classifier to the exec approval policy and wires it into the main gateway-host, node-host, and direct `system.run` approval paths. The guard forces explicit approval for OpenClaw lifecycle mutations unless exec is already in yolo mode (`security=full`, `ask=off`).

Foreground gateway runtime forms such as `openclaw gateway`, `openclaw gateway run`, `openclaw gateway --force`, and option-only gateway run surfaces such as `--port` are treated as lifecycle mutations. Read-only inspection remains outside the guard, including `openclaw gateway status`, `openclaw gateway --help`, `openclaw gateway run --help`, `launchctl print`, `systemctl status`, `schtasks /Query`, and generic read-only process lookups. `openclaw gateway call` is method-aware: lifecycle RPCs such as `update.run` and `gateway.restart.request` require explicit lifecycle approval, while read-only RPCs such as `health`, `update.status`, and `logs.tail` do not.

## User Impact

Operators get an extra human confirmation before an agent or auto-review path can stop, start, restart, run, delete, or uninstall the OpenClaw gateway/daemon in non-yolo configurations. Existing yolo-mode behavior and read-only status/query commands are unchanged.

## Evidence

Final branch head validated: `8886ea5462a3`.

Before/source proof: current `main` only hard-gated the existing security-audit suppression case before generic ask/allowlist/auto-review handling. OpenClaw lifecycle mutations were not classified before durable allowlist or auto-review decisions in the gateway-host, node-host, or `system.run` paths.

target.title: feat(daylog): automatic work journal plugin with Control UI timeline tab
target.body:
Closes #99867

## What Problem This Solves

There is no way to look back at a day and see what you actually did on your machine. Time trackers log app names; they miss what the work was. Dayflow (MIT, standalone macOS app) proved the recipe — periodic screen capture, vision-model observation, timeline synthesis — but as a separate app its output is locked away from the assistant.

This PR adds **Daylog**, a bundled (disabled-by-default) plugin that turns screen snapshots from a paired node into a reviewable timeline of the day, surfaced in a new Control UI sidebar tab, with a daily-standup generator and timeline-grounded Q&A.

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenClaw already owns every capability the idea needs — node screen capture, media-understanding providers, plugin services, gateway RPC, plugin SQLite state, the dashboard. Composing them as a plugin keeps the data local, makes it queryable by the assistant later, and exercises existing seams:

- **Capture**: a plugin service invokes `screen.snapshot` (app nodes) or the new plugin-provided `daylog.snapshot` node-host command (headless macOS node hosts, backed by `screencapture`/`sips`) every `captureIntervalSeconds` (default 30s). A node-invoke policy adds `daylog.snapshot` to the default macOS allowlist while the plugin is enabled. Identical consecutive frames are marked idle and excluded from analysis.
- **Two-stage analysis** (Dayflow-style): elapsed windows (default 15 min, split at >2 min gaps) go to a structured-extraction vision model (`api.runtime.mediaUnderstanding.extractStructuredWithModel`, e.g. `codex/gpt-5.5`) producing timestamped observations; observations plus a 45-minute lookback of existing cards are revised into 10-60 min timeline cards via `api.runtime.llm.complete` (default agent model), with one JSON-repair retry. Cards are a revisable draft: later batches may restructure the recent window.
- **Storage**: plugin-owned SQLite (`node:sqlite`, same pattern as memory-core/imessage) under `<state-dir>/daylog/`; frames pruned after `retentionDays` (default 14); batches stuck in `running` reset to `pending` on restart.
- **UI**: new `Daylog` tab following the Workboard/Dreams precedent (core view calling plugin-registered `daylog.*` gateway methods; plugin-disabled callout when off). Timeline cards with category colors, keyframe snapshots, distraction chips; day stats; standup generator; ask-your-day box.

Architecture notes: owner boundary respected (all product logic in `extensions/daylog`; the core diff is generic tab wiring + i18n). No new core config; plugin config has 8 clamped keys. Raw SQL is plugin-local DDL plus prepared statements, matching existing extension storage (the shared Kysely helpers are core-only).

## User Impact

- Off by default; no behavior change until `openclaw plugins enable daylog`.
- Once enabled: the Daylog tab shows the day as expandable activity cards with focus/category stats, one-click standup notes, and natural-language recall over the tracked day.
- Privacy: frames and the timeline stay on the gateway host; images leave only as analysis input to the operator-chosen model; the headless capture command is only advertised/allowlisted while the plugin is enabled.

## Evidence

- Unit tests: `extensions/daylog/src/analyze.test.ts` (time parsing, JSON repair contract, overlap trimming, batch windowing/gap split, sampling, keyframe pick) and `extensions/daylog/src/store.test.ts` (idle exclusion, crash recovery, revision-window replacement, stats, retention pruning) — 21 tests green via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/daylog`.
- Contract suites green: `src/plugins/contracts/package-manifest.contract.test.ts`, `src/plugins/contracts/extension-runtime-dependencies.contract.test.ts`, `src/plugins/bundled-plugin-naming.test.ts`, `test/extension-import-boundaries.test.ts`.
- `pnpm build` green (bundled plugin dist + control UI assets); `pnpm tsgo` + `pnpm tsgo:extensions` green; scoped oxlint green; `pnpm ui:i18n:sync` regenerated locales.
- **Live end-to-end on macOS** (isolated-state dev gateway + headless node host from this branch): node paired with `daylog.snapshot` in its approved surface; real screen frames captured every 10s (19+ frames, idle detection active); analysis batches ran against real `codex/gpt-5.5` (`chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses` transport) producing timestamped observations and merged timeline cards that correctly described the on-screen work; the Daylog tab rendered cards with keyframe snapshots, day stats (focus bar, categories, apps), a generated Daily Standup (Done/Today/Blockers), and an answered ask-your-day question. Live-test screenshots contain personal screen content and were reviewed locally instead of being attached.
- The live test also hardened the plugin: node-invoke policy allowlisting, `node.invoke` payload-envelope unwrapping, node-inventory diagnostics in capture errors, and config-snapshot loading for the tab were all found and fixed against the running gateway.

Release-note context: feat(plugins): add Daylog automatic work journal plugin with Control UI timeline tab (screen snapshots via paired nodes, Dayflow-style two-stage analysis, daily standup, ask-your-day).

target.title: fix: inbound messages can be reprocessed after gateway restart or reconnect (persistent replay dedupe + bounded durable replay)
target.body:
Fixes #97538
Part of #69208

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where inbound messages could be **reprocessed after a gateway restart or channel reconnect**, producing duplicate agent runs and, in the worst case, an unrecoverable re-delivery storm:

- **Discord / LINE / Mattermost**: the inbound replay dedupe guard was memory-only, so any event the platform re-delivers across a restart (Discord gateway resume, LINE webhook retry, Mattermost websocket replay) was processed again as a fresh message. Sibling channels (Telegram, iMessage, Nextcloud Talk) already persist this guard.
- **WhatsApp (#97538, Bug 2)**: the durable inbound journal replayed *all* pending events on every reconnect with no attempt accounting, no cap, and no dead-letter (pending TTL: 30 days). A poison event — e.g. a heavy multimodal batch whose run stalls before `complete()` — re-delivered on every reconnect forever, and restarting the gateway (the intuitive remediation) re-triggered the storm.

#97538's **Bug 1** (`abort_embedded_run` with `released=0`, owner lock never freed) is the same defect as #91700 and was already fixed by #91802 (`f194be19e2`, shipped in v2026.6.10/v2026.6.11); the reporter was on v2026.6.5. With Bug 1 fixed, the remaining live defect on `main` was the unbounded replay this PR removes. Asks 3 (ingress drain/ack CLI verb) and 4 (replay age threshold) from #97538 are operator/product decisions left to maintainers.

## Why This Change Was Made

One theme: **inbound accept must be idempotent and bounded across restarts**, enforced at the existing chokepoints instead of per-channel patches.

- The three memory-only channels flip to the existing SDK persistent claimable dedupe (`createClaimableDedupe` with `pluginId`/`namespacePrefix`), exactly the shape Telegram/iMessage already use. TTLs and in-memory caps are preserved per channel.
- The durable inbound receive journal (C3 chokepoint, `src/channels/message/durable-receive.ts`) gains its missing terminal state — `fail()` (queue-backed: proper `failed` tombstone via the ingress queue; store-backed: terminal tombstone) — and a canonical `replayPendingDurableInboundReceives({ journal, maxAttempts, process })` helper that counts each replay attempt *before* processing (so stalls and crashes still converge), skips records whose row vanished between the pending snapshot and the attempt (concurrent complete/prune → no stale double-delivery), isolates per-record processing errors (one poison record cannot starve the rest of the pass), and dead-letters at the cap. WhatsApp's inline replay loop is deleted in favor of the helper (`WHATSAPP_DURABLE_INBOUND_MAX_REPLAY_ATTEMPTS = 5`, a bound on total delivery attempts). No new config surface; the shared `channel_ingress_events` queue already had `attempts` and `fail()` — WhatsApp just never used them (Telegram's ingress spool already does).
- The three flipped guards wire `onDiskError` warning logs (persistent dedupe fails open on storage errors; without the hook a broken state DB silently downgrades to memory-only), matching the telegram/nextcloud-talk/raft precedent.
- Test infrastructure: persistent dedupe means suites that reuse fixed message ids need per-test state isolation (`--isolate=false` safety). A shared `installIsolatedPluginStateDirForTests` helper (SDK test runtime) replaces per-suite hand-rolled scaffolds and is applied to the five affected suites, including `message-handler.bot-self-filter.test.ts` which was committing fixed ids through the real guard.

Non-goals: the ingress drain/ack operator verb and reconnect age-threshold policy (asks 3/4 of #97538), and the stale-claim startup sweep (#90989 covers that separately).

Overlap disclosure: open PR #86577 pursues the same intent for the Discord slice (persist the inbound replay guard) but via a file-backed state dir, which predates the plugin-state SQLite migration and conflicts with the current "SQLite only" storage policy; it has failing CI and is waiting on author. This PR covers that surface with the canonical SQLite plugin-state path (the same shape Telegram/iMessage use). If this lands, #86577 should be closed as superseded.

## User Impact

- Discord, LINE, and Mattermost users no longer receive duplicate agent replies when the platform re-delivers an inbound event across a gateway restart.
- WhatsApp deployments can no longer wedge into the #97538 restart-amplified re-delivery loop: a pending inbound event is replayed at most 5 times across reconnects, then dead-lettered with a warning log (`dropping durable WhatsApp inbound after max replay attempts`), keeping the lane healthy. Successfully processed events are unaffected (they complete as before and never replay).

## Evidence

- TDD: every fix landed RED→GREEN.
  - `extensions/discord/src/monitor/inbound-dedupe.test.ts`, `extensions/line/src/webhook-replay-persist.test.ts`, `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/inbound-replay-persist.test.ts`: a committed replay key on a fresh guard instance (= restart) now reports `duplicate` (fails on memory-only guards).
  - `src/channels/message/durable-receive.test.ts` (+6): `fail()` dead-letters on both journal flavors and blocks re-accept; bounded replay processes fresh records, records attempts across stalled replays (`attempts` 1 → 2 → dead-letter at cap), dead-letters poison events, isolates a throwing record while still replaying the rest, and skips a record whose row vanished before the attempt was recorded.
- Suites (post-rebase onto `upstream/main`): WhatsApp **986/986**, Discord **1832/1832**, LINE **292/292**, `src/channels/message/` **171/171**, `src/plugin-state/` **34/34**; mattermost green except `client.retry.test.ts`, which fails identically on the branch base (pre-existing, unrelated HTTP-retry suite).
- `pnpm build` clean; `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:extensions:test` clean; `plugin-sdk:api:check` OK (baseline regenerated for the new exports); oxfmt/oxlint clean.
- An 8-angle multi-agent self-review ran on the branch; accepted findings (release-return guard, poison-record isolation, `onDiskError` logging, test state-dir isolation, SDK-surface trims, API baseline) are fixed in the final commit.
- `codex review --base upstream/main` ran locally (per CONTRIBUTING); its single P2 finding — adding a required `fail` method to the shipped `DurableInboundReceiveJournal` SDK type would break external implementers — is addressed: the shipped type is untouched and both factories now return a `DurableInboundReceiveReplayableJournal` intersection that carries `fail`.
- Import-boundary inventories clean (`check-src-extension-import-boundary`, `check-sdk-package-extension-import-boundary` both `[]`); `pnpm test:contracts` 955 passed with 2 failures under triage as pre-existing (evidence below if confirmed).
- Pre-existing, unrelated failure noted for reviewers: `src/plugin-sdk/provider-catalog-shared.test.ts` (2 tests, native streaming usage compat) fails standalone with impl+test byte-identical to base `6cb82eaab8`.
- Known follow-ups deliberately not in this PR: persistent-dedupe per-message SQLite write cost is the same as the existing telegram/imessage guards (amortizing the eviction sweep is a separate perf change); the journal facade's prune-per-release/complete transaction amplification predates this PR; `createClaimableDedupe` defaults `stateMaxEntries` to 1 when omitted (all callers here pass it explicitly).
- SDK contract: `DurableInboundReceiveJournal` (`accept`/`pending`/`complete`/`release`, now `fail`) was already public API through `channel-outbound` — WhatsApp's inbound monitor consumes it from that exact barrel pre-dating this PR. This PR documents the full facade (`docs/plugins/sdk-channel-outbound.md`, "Durable Inbound Receive" section, including "don't build a channel-local dedupe/spool" guidance) and regenerates `docs/docs_map.md`. This is also the intended next step for other channels: Telegram's `extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-spool.ts` reimplements the same accept/attempt/dead-letter shape as a channel-local spool and is still accumulating bespoke fixes (as recently as 2 days before this PR) rather than converging on the shared journal — no open PR proposes that consolidation, so keeping this documented and public now avoids reopening the same surface-budget/docs conversation per channel.

**Real gateway restart-replay proof (LINE)** (details + logs in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/99365#issuecomment-4872867728)): on a real local gateway built from this branch (isolated `$HOME`, LINE channel, signed webhooks), event `m-proof-1` was delivered and processed, the gateway process was killed and restarted, and the platform-style redelivery of the same event was **deduped across the restart** (`line: skipped replayed webhook event message:m-proof-1`) while a fresh event was processed normally; both replay keys are visible in `plugin_state_entries` (`line.webhook-replay.*`).

Discord and Mattermost flip the exact same shared SDK mechanism (`createClaimableDedupe` with `pluginId`/`namespacePrefix`) that LINE's live proof exercises — only the channel-specific admission/webhook wrapper differs. An equivalent live-gateway demo was attempted for both and is not included here:
- **Discord**: not practically reproducible without a live bot account — its inbound transport is a persistent WebSocket the process opens *outward* to Discord's real servers, so there is no local endpoint to POST a forged redelivery to.
- **Mattermost**: technically reproducible (baseUrl/token are plugin config, so a local fake Mattermost server can stand in), but the attempt hit an unrelated dev-harness artifact (`scripts/run-node.mjs` hot-reloads the channel plugin ~10s after startup even on a fresh build, racing the test push against the reload) rather than a product-code issue.

Both channels have their own real, SQLite-backed regression tests exercising the identical persistent guard through the actual channel handler (not a mock): `extensions/discord/src/monitor/inbound-dedupe.test.ts` and `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.bot-self-filter.test.ts` (drives the real `createDiscordMessageHandler`), and `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/inbound-replay-persist.test.ts`.

**Real cross-process proof of the WhatsApp bounded-replay fix.** WhatsApp's durable-inbound replay trigger is local (it fires on socket attach against on-disk pending state, not on a live platform round-trip), so this mechanism was exercised directly with the actual shipped code from this branch — `src/channels/message/durable-receive.ts` and the exact `WHATSAPP_DURABLE_INBOUND_MAX_REPLAY_ATTEMPTS` constant from `extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/durable-receive.ts`, imported and run, not mocked — as **3 separate `node` process invocations**, each with its own module state, against one real on-disk SQLite state dir. This models 3 separate gateway reconnects, including a genuine process kill mid-turn:

Setup (seed): one healthy pending record (`healthy-1`) and one "poison" record (`poison-1`) pre-advanced to `attempts=4` — the exact pre-storm state #97538 describes (a backlog that has already survived several failed reconnect replays).

*Reconnect 1* (new process): `healthy-1` processes and completes normally. `poison-1`'s handler is made to hang forever (models #97538 Bug 1's wedged `embedded_run` lane) — the process is killed via a 3s timeout instead of waiting forever, the same way a real gateway restart would end a wedged run:
```
[phase 1] force-exiting after 3s (simulated crash while poison-1 was wedged)
```
SQLite after the kill: `healthy-1|completed|1`, `poison-1|pending|5`. The attempt was counted (4→5) *before* the crash, because `release()` runs before `process()` in the bounded-replay helper — a stall still converges on the cap instead of resetting the count.

*Reconnect 2* (new process): `poison-1` is now at the cap and is dead-lettered without ever calling its handler again — no further storm:
```
[phase 2] dropping durable WhatsApp inbound after max replay attempts: id=poison-1 attempts=5
[phase 2] pending after replay: []
```

*Reconnect 3* (new process): stays dead — pending is empty, and a simulated platform redelivery of the same id (WhatsApp commonly resends via multi-device/offline sync) is recognized as already-terminal and not reprocessed:
```
[phase 3] redelivery of dead-lettered poison-1 => kind=pending duplicate=true
```
Final state: `healthy-1|completed|1`, `poison-1|failed|5` — the healthy message delivered normally throughout, the poison message stopped storming after exactly 5 total attempts and never came back.

#97538 Bug 1 provenance for reviewers: `f194be19e2` ("fix(diagnostics): release wedged session lane when stuck recovery aborts with queued session work", #91802, fixes #91700) is contained in v2026.6.10+ (`gh api repos/openclaw/openclaw/compare/v2026.6.10...f194be19e2` → `behind`).

target.title: feat: pair mobile devices from the Control UI
target.body:
Related: #94661

## What Problem This Solves

The OpenClaw iOS/Android apps can scan a Gateway setup QR, but the Control UI could not create one. Operators had to leave the browser and use `openclaw qr` or the optional Telegram `device-pair` plugin; the UI exposed only the separate device-management surface.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds the hidden, `operator.admin`-scoped `device.pair.setupCode` RPC from the original contribution and uses it for a guided **Nodes → Pair mobile device** flow. The RPC reuses the canonical pairing/setup-code helpers; the Control UI adds no second token or QR format. The Devices card now appears at the top of Nodes, the dialog handles scan/copy/retry states, and the docs lead with the browser flow.

The setup code contains a short-lived bootstrap credential. The RPC returns only the opaque setup code plus non-secret connection metadata, is not advertised, and keeps the configured `device-pair` public URL fallback used by the existing CLI/plugin flow.

## User Impact

An already paired administrator can now connect a phone without opening a terminal:

1. Open **Nodes** in the Control UI.
2. Click **Pair mobile device**.
3. In the mobile app, open **Settings → Gateway** and scan the QR (or paste the setup code).
4. The official app connects automatically. If **Devices** shows a pending request, review its role and scopes before approving it.

Sessions without `operator.admin` cannot create setup codes. Remote pairing still requires a secure/reachable Gateway URL (`wss://`, such as Tailscale Serve/Funnel); private LAN and loopback retain their existing allowances.

## Evidence

- Visual proof: mocked before/after screenshots and a short flow recording captured locally; attachment upload is pending because the Crabbox artifact broker is not configured and the existing-Chrome bridge is offline
- Focused Gateway + Control UI tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/device-pair-setup.test.ts ui/src/ui/views/nodes.devices.test.ts`

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `/thinking high|low|medium` was rejected with "not supported for github-copilot/claude-sonnet-4.6, use one of: off" for dynamically-discovered Copilot Claude models, even though the backing Claude model supports reasoning. Only `off` was advertised.

## Why This Change Was Made

Copilot's `/models` endpoint does not expose OpenAI-style `reasoning_effort` for Anthropic-backed models, so model discovery marks every Copilot-discovered Claude model `reasoning: false`. The shared thinking resolver (`src/auto-reply/thinking.ts`) then discarded github-copilot's declared level set and fell back to off-only, because neither thinking surface set `preserveWhenCatalogReasoningFalse`. This PR sets that flag for Claude models (detected via the existing `anthropic-messages` transport signal) on BOTH github-copilot thinking surfaces, mirroring `anthropic`, `amazon-bedrock`, `google`, and `moonshot`:
- the active provider hook (`resolveThinkingProfile` in `index.ts`), and
- the bundled provider-policy surface (`provider-policy-api.ts`, used by `/think`, ACP controls, and directive parsing when no active plugin supplies the hook).

This preserves the levels the hooks already declare (`off/minimal/low/medium/high`) and invents no new ones; non-Claude Copilot models without `reasoning_effort` stay off-only.

Per review on #99240: both thinking surfaces must agree before merge.

## User Impact

Users running Copilot-routed Claude models (e.g. `claude-sonnet-4.6`, `claude-opus-4.7`) can use `/thinking high|low|medium` as expected, instead of being locked to `off` — across the active provider path and the bundled/directive path.

target.title: fix(voice-call): resolve completed calls from the persisted store on status misses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where voice-call status lookups reported `{ found: false }` for calls that had completed successfully and had a full transcript persisted to disk. Once a call was evicted from the in-memory call manager (after finalize, a gateway restart, or max-duration expiry), the lookups only checked memory and never fell back to the persisted store, so the agent/operator could not retrieve the conversation.

## Why This Change Was Made

All FOUR status-lookup sites now fall back to the persisted call history when the in-memory manager has no entry, resolving the NEWEST matching snapshot:
- the `voicecall.status` gateway method,
- the `voice_call` tool `get_status` action,
- the legacy `mode: "status"` tool branch, and
- the local CLI `voicecall status` gateway-unavailable fallback.

History is returned oldest-first, so the lookup uses `toReversed().find(...)` — a forward `find()` would return a stale/older snapshot. This mirrors the existing `describeHistoricalCall` helper. The CLI fallback previously consulted only `getCall(callId)` (narrower than the gateway path), so it now also consults `getCallByProviderCallId`, aligning all four readers.

Per review on #96586: the CLI path must agree with the gateway/tool paths, so the CLI fallback is included here rather than split out. Note the existing stalled PR #96624 takes the same direction but selects the oldest snapshot via `events.find()`; this change resolves the newest snapshot instead.

## User Impact

Operators and agents can retrieve the status and transcript of completed voice calls after they leave the in-memory manager (e.g. after a gateway restart or enough time has passed), from the tool, the gateway, or the CLI — instead of a dead-end `{ found: false }`.

## Evidence

- `extensions/voice-call/index.test.ts`: two regression tests — newest snapshot wins over an older `ringing` record; `{ found: false }` when absent.
- `extensions/voice-call/src/cli.test.ts`: two integration tests drive the real `voicecall status --call-id ... --json` command with the gateway unavailable (ECONNREFUSED) and an evicted call — asserting the CLI fallback resolves the newest persisted snapshot (`state: completed`) and reports `{ found: false }` when neither active nor persisted. This exercises the actual CLI action end-to-end (only the gateway transport and the in-memory manager are stubbed).
- `pnpm test:extension voice-call`: `index.test.ts` 41/41 and `cli.test.ts` 10/10 pass. The full extension suite only has pre-existing Windows `EPERM` teardown flakes in `src/manager/events.test.ts` (temp-dir `fs.rmSync`), unrelated to this change.

target.title: fix(discord): fall back to text-only when media upload exceeds Discord size limit
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an agent reply includes a media attachment larger than Discord's bot upload limit, the entire outbound reply (text AND attachment) is rejected by Discord with HTTP 413 and **silently lost**. The user sees the agent as simply not responding. Dispatch still reports `outcome=completed`, so monitoring doesn't catch it either.

Production evidence from issue #99021: a 10.7 MB MP3 attachment caused the same 413 failure twice, with the channel effectively wedged for that reply.

Fixes #99021

## Changes

**1. Lower `DEFAULT_DISCORD_MEDIA_MAX_MB` from 100 to 25** (`send.outbound.ts`)

Discord's base-tier upload cap is 25 MB. The previous 100 MB default meant files up to 100 MB passed OpenClaw's preflight check but Discord rejected them at upload. Users with boosted servers (50/100 MB limits) can still override via the existing `mediaMaxMb` config option.

- Detects the 413 via `getDiscordErrorStatus()` (existing utility in the same file)
- Falls back to `sendDiscordText()` with the full original text plus a note: *⚠️ Attachment could not be delivered — it exceeds Discord's upload size limit.*

target.title: fix(subagents): killed subagent runs stay running in the task list
target.body:
Related: #90444

## What Problem This Solves

Killing a running subagent ended the subagent-registry entry but left its detached task row `running` indefinitely. Task surfaces therefore disagreed with the control result.

## Why This Change Was Made

All direct, admin, cascade, and parent-abort kill paths converge on `markSubagentRunTerminated`. The fix finalizes the matching task there. It also preserves the existing kill/completion race contract in either callback order: only a session-backed subagent may reconcile `cancelled` to authoritative `succeeded`; other runtime cancellations stay sticky. Owner delivery says `cancellation requested`, which remains true if the final reply wins the race.

## User Impact

Newly killed subagent tasks no longer remain phantom `running` rows. A final reply that genuinely completes during cancellation still wins and clears the stale kill error.

## Evidence

Production-path live trace using real `registerSubagentRun`, `killSubagentRunAdmin`, task persistence, task listing, and owner system-event delivery in an isolated state directory:

Before (`main`):

```text
spawned: running / pending
kill: found=true killed=true
killed: running / pending
owner event: none
late completion: succeeded
```

After:

```text
spawned: running / pending
kill: found=true killed=true
killed: cancelled / session_queued / "Subagent run killed."
owner event: "Background task cancellation requested: Subagent task (run run-live)."
late completion: succeeded / error cleared
```

Focused validation:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/subagent-control.test.ts src/tasks/task-registry.test.ts src/tasks/task-executor-policy.test.ts` — 122 passed.
- Fresh Codex autoreview — clean, 0.93 confidence.
- Rebased onto current `main`; exact-head CI follows on the pushed head.

## Scope

This fixes new kill finalization. #90444 remains open for historical stuck rows, child CLI rows, timestamp repair, and maintenance reconciliation.

target.title: fix(plugins): publish git installs across devices
target.body:
Closes #99885

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users installing git-backed plugins in Docker or other split-filesystem setups would hit `EXDEV: cross-device link not permitted` when OpenClaw tried to publish the cloned repository from the process temp directory into the managed git plugin directory.

## Why This Change Was Made

The managed git repo publish step now keeps the existing backup/restore behavior but uses the existing cross-device-safe move helper for both backup and final publish moves. That preserves the previous rollback semantics while allowing the final staged clone to be copied through the helper when a direct rename cannot cross filesystems.

## User Impact

Users can install `git:` plugins when `/tmp` and the OpenClaw state directory live on different mounts, such as Docker containers with bind-mounted home or state directories. Existing install failure behavior and security success events remain unchanged when publishing fails.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: git plugin install publishing falls back successfully when the final managed repo rename raises `EXDEV`, while still emitting the install success event only after the repo is published.
- Commands / artifacts:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/git-install.test.ts` -> 21 tests passed.

## Summary

This PR adds first-class `google-antigravity` support through the Antigravity `agy --print` runtime and hardens the surrounding Google auth replacement boundary.

- `google-antigravity` uses the signed-in Antigravity / `agy` session.
- `google-gemini-cli` uses the official Gemini CLI OAuth cache.

OpenClaw already separates Google API-key auth, Gemini CLI OAuth, and provider-owned runtime auth paths, but it did not have a first-class Antigravity provider path. This PR adds `google-antigravity` as a provider-owned CLI runtime path. target.title: fix(outbound): message tool reports success while best-effort delivery failed
target.body:
Related: #84232

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where agents using the `message` tool to reply in the current conversation would see a normal, success-shaped result even when channel delivery actually failed or partially failed.

For channels that deliver agent replies through the message tool (`message_tool_only` mode — Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Telegram, and others), implicit current-source replies are forced to best-effort sends (#84232). In that mode `sendMessage()` discards the durable batch send outcome: a total delivery failure returns an envelope with no failure signal at all, and a partial failure (for example chunk 2 of 3 rejected) returns the last successfully delivered chunk's `messageId` — indistinguishable from a fully successful send. The agent believes the reply reached the user and keeps acting on that assumption.

The safety net that is supposed to catch this already exists: `deliveryEnvelopeIndicatesPartialDelivery` in `src/agents/embedded-agent-message-tool-source-reply.ts` checks tool result envelopes for `deliveryStatus: "partial_failed"` / `sentBeforeError`. But this send path never emitted those fields, so the detector could never fire.

## Why This Change Was Made

`MessageSendResult.deliveryStatus` is widened from only `"suppressed"` to `"sent" | "suppressed" | "partial_failed" | "failed"`, and the direct-send return in `sendMessage()` now populates it from the durable batch send result, together with a formatted `error`, `sentBeforeError`, and serialized per-payload `payloadOutcomes`. The derivation mirrors `deliveryStatusFromDurableSend` in `src/agents/command/delivery.ts`, which already projects the same durable send result honestly for agent command replies.

Throw semantics are intentionally unchanged: best-effort sends still resolve instead of throwing (the #84232 contract), and non-best-effort failures still throw. This change only makes the resolved envelope tell the truth. Non-goals: the best-effort policy itself, the partial-delivery detector, and the result shapes of the gateway-relayed and dry-run branches are untouched.

## User Impact

Agents (and anything else consuming message tool send results) can now distinguish a delivered reply from a dropped or partially delivered one. The already-shipped partial-delivery detection in the source-reply flow becomes effective for this path, so a failed visible reply is no longer silently treated as delivered. Successful sends now also carry an explicit `deliveryStatus: "sent"`; existing fields are unchanged.

## Evidence

Real-runtime capture (`node --import tsx`, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, no mocks — the bundled Telegram plugin makes a real HTTPS call to `api.telegram.org` with an invalid bot token, so the send genuinely fails at the platform boundary with `401: Unauthorized`).

Before this change — the channel logs `message failed: Call to 'sendMessage' failed! (401: Unauthorized)`, yet the agent-visible envelope is success-shaped:

```json
{
  "channel": "telegram",
  "to": "123456789",
  "via": "direct",
  "mediaUrl": null
}
```

After this change — same real 401, same call, envelope now reports the failure:

```json
{
  "channel": "telegram",
  "to": "123456789",
  "via": "direct",
  "mediaUrl": null,
  "deliveryStatus": "failed",
  "error": "Call to 'sendMessage' failed! (401: Unauthorized)",
  "payloadOutcomes": [
    {
      "index": 0,
      "status": "failed",
      "error": "Call to 'sendMessage' failed! (401: Unauthorized)",
      "sentBeforeError": false,
      "stage": "platform_send"
    }
  ]
}
```

Focused tests in `src/infra/outbound/message.test.ts` (all passing via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/outbound/message.test.ts`), written failing-first against the old behavior:

- best-effort total failure: still does not throw, now carries `deliveryStatus: "failed"` plus `error` and the failed payload outcome (previously indistinguishable from success)
- best-effort partial failure with one of two payloads sent: `deliveryStatus: "partial_failed"`, `sentBeforeError: true`, per-payload outcomes, `result` still the last delivered chunk
- regression: plain success reports `deliveryStatus: "sent"`; suppressed sends keep `deliveryStatus: "suppressed"`

Typecheck (`pnpm tsgo`), lint/format on the touched files, and the adjacent `src/infra/outbound/message-action-runner.core-send.test.ts` suite also pass locally. Running the entire `src/infra/outbound/` test directory in one process is flaky on the local dev machine independent of this change (the same files fail on an unmodified checkout of the merge-base commit, with different failure sets across runs; each file passes when run on its own) — broad verification is deferred to CI.

target.title: feat: embedded operator terminal — gateway foundation + web Control UI (1/3)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw deployments on WSL, Docker, or remote servers have no built-in shell: to run a command alongside the assistant you switch to a separate SSH client or device, breaking the Control UI's single-pane-of-glass. This adds an embedded operator terminal — a real PTY-backed shell — to the Control UI, and lays the gateway foundation the iOS and Android apps build on next.

Closes #77362.

**PR 1 of 3** (foundation + web UI). PR 2 adds the iOS Terminal tab, PR 3 adds Android; both consume the gateway `terminal.*` protocol introduced here (served as a full-screen terminal page for their WebViews).

## Why This Change Was Made

Prior attempts informed the design:
- #28691 (closed to the stale-bot, not on merits) proved the xterm.js + per-connection PTY RPC shape works. We keep that session model but use **ghostty-web** — Ghostty's real VT core compiled to WASM (xterm.js-compatible API) — instead of xterm.js, per maintainer preference.
- #52493 was **rejected for security**: it routed shells through a generic `exec.run`, so any `operator.write` client could run `{command:"sh",args:["-c",…]}` = arbitrary RCE. We deliberately avoid that trap — the terminal is a dedicated `terminal.*` method family gated to `operator.admin`, never a general command-exec seam.

## User Impact

- A **dockable** terminal panel in the Control UI — a real bottom bar or right sidebar that reshapes the content (the chat reflows to make room; it is not an overlay), toggled with the toolbar button or **Ctrl+`**, with multiple session tabs. The bottom dock follows the shell layout, aligning to the nav rail when collapsed and spanning full width on narrow/mobile viewports.
- Each session starts in the target agent's workspace.
- **Workspace isolation mirrors the agent's own sandbox, fail-closed:** with no sandbox (`off`, the default) you get a host shell that can navigate the whole filesystem. Under `non-main` the agent's main session already runs on the host, so a host terminal is allowed there too. Only a **fully-sandboxed agent (`sandbox.mode: "all"`)** is refused rather than handed an unconfined host shell — running the terminal *inside* an active sandbox is a tracked follow-up.
- Enabled by default; `gateway.terminal.enabled: false` is a kill switch, `gateway.terminal.shell` overrides the shell. Changing `gateway.terminal.*` **restarts the gateway** (like other `gateway.*` config): the terminal drives the Control UI CSP and bootstrap availability — both fixed at document load — plus live PTYs, none of which can hot-update a connected client. The restart kills every live PTY and clients reconnect with the correct page state.

## Security

A browser-authenticated host shell is an RCE-class surface (per the #77362 review), so:
- **Admin-only.** All `terminal.*` methods (and the `terminal.data`/`terminal.exit` event streams) require `operator.admin` — the same bar as `config.set`. An authenticated admin operator can already edit config and drive agents to exec, so this adds convenience, not new authority. The Control UI mirrors this: the toolbar toggle and dock only appear for a **live, admin** connection, and the panel tears its tabs down on disconnect rather than pointing input at server-killed sessions.
- **Not `exec.run`.** Dedicated methods; no arbitrary command routing (contrast #52493).
- **Fail-closed isolation.** A fully-sandboxed agent (`sandbox.mode: "all"`) is refused, never downgraded to a host shell. Explicit agent ids are validated against the configured agent list first — an unknown id is rejected rather than silently resolved against global defaults (which would sidestep a per-agent sandbox refusal).
- **Lifecycle-bound.** Sessions are pinned to the opening connection, killed on disconnect and on gateway shutdown (process-tree kill, so child commands don't orphan); a per-gateway session cap bounds process use.
- **Scoped CSP relaxation.** ghostty-web's WASM needs `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` + `data:` in `connect-src`; these are added to the Control UI CSP **only when the terminal is enabled**, so the baseline policy stays tight. A page served while disabled reloads itself once if the flag flips on (the bootstrap refetch after the enabling restart detects it), since headers can't change on a live document.
- **Auditable.** Each open logs agent, session id, connection, and shell. **Kill switch:** `gateway.terminal.enabled: false` restarts the gateway (killing all live PTYs and reloading clients with the tight CSP); the RPC handlers also re-check config as an independent backstop and close any session that receives input while disabled.

## Architecture

- **Protocol** (`packages/gateway-protocol`): `terminal.open/input/resize/close` methods + `terminal.data/terminal.exit` events, additive; generated schema + Swift models regenerated.
- **Gateway** (`src/gateway/terminal/*`): `TerminalSessionManager` owns one `@lydell/node-pty` PTY per session and streams bytes to only the owning connection; `resolveTerminalLaunch` resolves agent → workspace → shell and enforces the fail-closed isolation rule.
- **Config**: `gateway.terminal.{enabled,shell}` with types, zod schema, labels, help; changes route through the standard `gateway.*` restart rule (no bespoke hot-reload machinery).
- **Control UI** (`ui/src/ui/terminal/*`): `<openclaw-terminal-panel>` (dockable bottom/right, resizable, session tabs) driving ghostty-web; `TerminalConnection` is the DOM-free protocol layer that subscribes to the shared gateway event stream only while sessions exist (failed opens and panel teardown release the listener, so reconnect cycles never accumulate subscriptions). ghostty-web is dynamically imported so its ~0.6 MB WASM chunk never weighs down the initial bundle. The dock publishes its footprint as CSS vars so the shell content reserves space instead of being overlaid.

## Evidence

- **Live end-to-end** (headless Chromium against a real gateway): opened the terminal from the toolbar, ran `pwd && ls && echo …` and `whoami && uname -sr` in both bottom and right docks and in a second session tab — real zsh prompt, workspace listing, and command output rendered; verified the content area shrinks (no overlap) when docked. Two integration bugs were caught and fixed this way: the Control UI CSP blocked the WASM load, and `terminal.data`/`terminal.exit` weren't in the gateway's event-scope guard so output never reached the client.
- **Unit tests**: session manager (open/input/resize/exit/disconnect/cap, concurrent-open cap, orphan-abort on disconnect-during-spawn, spawn-failure, silent dispose-all on shutdown), launch resolver (host plan, `non-main` allowed, `all` refused, shell resolution), CSP builder (wasm relaxation gated), kill switch (disabled `terminal.input`/`terminal.resize` close the session and reject; `gateway.terminal.*` config changes classify as gateway restart), UI availability predicate (gated on live connection + `operator.admin` scope + advertised method; unavailable while disconnected or for non-admin operators), UI connection layer (event routing, early-event buffering + replay for the open race, exit self-release/no-leak, unsubscribe on close/failed-open/dispose), advertised-method-order stability.
- **Responsive dock verified** headlessly against the real shell CSS: the bottom dock's left edge resolves to 258px (nav expanded), 78px (collapsed rail), and 0px (<1100px / mobile), instead of a fixed 258px that used to gap the collapsed layout and waste most of a phone viewport.
- **Reviewed** across many rounds of adversarial code review; the lifecycle was hardened for the open/exit races, the per-gateway session cap under concurrent opens, orphaned PTYs on disconnect-during-spawn, failed-open phantom tabs, tab-closed-while-open-in-flight cancellation (the fresh session is closed instead of surviving invisibly), reconnect teardown, availability gating (live admin connection, not just the server-wide advertised-method list), gateway-client listener leaks on failed opens, live light/dark theme switching (ghostty-web 0.4.0 ignores `options.theme` after `open()`, so the panel drives `renderer.setTheme` + one forced full render — verified against the dependency source), persisted dock sizes clamped to the current viewport (load, drag, and window-resize), and the responsive dock offset. The config-change path was deliberately simplified from a bespoke hot-reload action to the standard gateway restart after review showed CSP/bootstrap can't hot-update a connected client.
- `tsgo` type-checks clean (core + UI test projects); `ui:i18n:check` clean; protocol schema + Swift models regenerated and committed; dynamic imports for `ghostty-web`/`node-pty` confirmed code-split (no static-import bundling). Full `pnpm build` / `pnpm ui:build` run in CI.

target.title: feat(plugins): add scoped credential broker
target.body:
Depends on #98536.

Closes #98549.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw plugins currently need plaintext credentials in plugin-visible runtime configuration before they can perform credentialed operations. For team digital employees, that makes it difficult to grant one approved operation without also exposing the underlying secret to plugin code, tool arguments, logs, errors, events, or transcripts.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds one manifest-declared credential broker boundary. The broker resolves a structured SecretRef only inside core, authorizes the request against the prepared agent, conversation/channel, sender, and capability profile from #98536, validates the fixed destination and request limits through the existing guarded network path, and returns a single-use opaque request handle to the owning plugin tool.

The first end-to-end consumer is the existing Tavily search/extract plugin path. Structured SecretRefs use the broker; existing literal and environment-backed configuration remains unchanged. Handles are process-local, expire after 30 seconds, are deterministically revocable and single-use, and do not survive restart. Missing scope or grant denies by default, with no plaintext fallback.

This intentionally does not add a second generic HTTP client, global environment injection, broad RBAC, a general egress policy system, or an admin UI. Those are deferred to later focused changes.

## User Impact

Operators can configure supported plugin credentials as SecretRefs and allow an approved plugin operation without delivering the plaintext credential to the model or plugin tool. Plugin authors receive a narrow opaque broker API rather than secret-resolution access.

Security-owner review remains required for the secrets documentation and broker boundary.

Related: #97115

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where isolated cron `agentTurn` jobs with configured model fallbacks could stop on an embedded primary model that returned a fallback-safe incomplete result, such as reasoning-only or empty visible output, instead of trying the next configured fallback model.

This covers the returned-result / zero-token failure mode reported in #97115. The separate shared AbortController timeout claim is a distinct terminal-timeout contract and is intentionally left out of this narrow PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

The isolated cron embedded path now passes the existing embedded result fallback classifier and exhausted-result merge helper into `runWithModelFallback`, matching the already-supported embedded fallback contract. The classifier is scoped away from CLI-backed execution providers so CLI runtimes continue to own their own terminal classification.

## User Impact

Scheduled embedded cron runs can now recover through the configured fallback chain when the primary candidate returns a fallback-safe incomplete result. Users should get the healthy fallback model's answer instead of a recurring generic "Agent couldn't generate a response" cron failure for that returned-result case.

target.title: fix(exec): require approval for OpenClaw lifecycle commands
target.body:
Fixes #99518

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where exec commands through gateway or node hosts could let OpenClaw gateway/daemon lifecycle mutations pass through normal allowlist or auto-review paths when they should require explicit approval.

The affected workflow is OpenClaw self-management from exec surfaces: stopping, starting, restarting, running, deleting, or uninstalling the gateway/daemon through CLI, launchctl, systemctl, schtasks, process-kill, shell-wrapper, package-manager, Windows shim, `env -S`, `xargs`/`find`, `sudo`/`doas`, and dispatch-wrapper commands.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a focused lifecycle classifier to the exec approval policy and wires it into the main gateway-host, node-host, and direct `system.run` approval paths. The guard forces explicit approval for OpenClaw lifecycle mutations unless exec is already in yolo mode (`security=full`, `ask=off`).

Foreground gateway runtime forms such as `openclaw gateway`, `openclaw gateway run`, `openclaw gateway --force`, and option-only gateway run surfaces such as `--port` are treated as lifecycle mutations. Read-only inspection remains outside the guard, including `openclaw gateway status`, `openclaw gateway --help`, `openclaw gateway run --help`, `launchctl print`, `systemctl status`, `schtasks /Query`, and generic read-only process lookups. `openclaw gateway call` is method-aware: lifecycle RPCs such as `update.run` and `gateway.restart.request` require explicit lifecycle approval, while read-only RPCs such as `health`, `update.status`, and `logs.tail` do not.

## User Impact

Operators get an extra human confirmation before an agent or auto-review path can stop, start, restart, run, delete, or uninstall the OpenClaw gateway/daemon in non-yolo configurations. Existing yolo-mode behavior and read-only status/query commands are unchanged.

## Evidence

Final branch head validated: `8886ea5462a3`.

Before/source proof: current `main` only hard-gated the existing security-audit suppression case before generic ask/allowlist/auto-review handling. OpenClaw lifecycle mutations were not classified before durable allowlist or auto-review decisions in the gateway-host, node-host, or `system.run` paths.

target.title: fix: recover stranded replies in message_tool_only mode (#85714)
target.body:
## Summary

When `messages.visibleReplies` is set to `message_tool`, the agent is expected to call the message tool to deliver replies. If the LLM forgets (a probabilistic event — the reporter saw it happen on the 8th turn after 7 correct deliveries), the reply was **silently discarded**: the substantive text sat in the JSONL transcript but was never delivered to the user.

The existing `shouldWarnAboutPrivateMessageToolFinal()` detection was already identifying these stranded replies and logging a warning, but took no recovery action.

## Fix

This commit promotes the detection from log-only to **followup retry**, preserving the `message_tool_only` privacy contract:

1. **Gate room events**: Skip stranded reply detection for ambient `room_event` turns where `message_tool_only` is automatically set by the system. Silence on room events is intentional by design — the agent chose not to respond.

2. **Enqueue followup retry turn**: When a stranded reply is detected, enqueue a followup run whose prompt instructs the agent to deliver the captured text via `message(action=send)`. The agent itself calls the message tool, so delivery happens through the correct contract path — no suppression bypass, no privacy boundary crossing.

3. **Clear transcript/persistence fields**: The retry run explicitly clears `transcriptPrompt`, `userTurnTranscriptRecorder`, and `currentInboundContext` from the original followup run to prevent the original user prompt from hiding the retry instruction. The followup runner resolves `transcriptPrompt ?? extracted.text`, so a retained `transcriptPrompt` would cause the agent to see the original user question instead of the retry delivery instruction.

4. **No suppression bypass**: This does NOT mark payloads with `deliverDespiteSourceReplySuppression` or use `skipSuppressionCheck`. The `message_tool_only` privacy contract is fully preserved: delivery only happens when the agent explicitly calls `message(action=send)`.

Normal (non-stranded) paths are unaffected: short replies, intentional `NO_REPLY`, and runs where the message tool already delivered are all excluded by the existing `shouldWarnAboutPrivateMessageToolFinal` guard.

### Why followup retry instead of bypass delivery?

The `message_tool_only` contract says: "no message tool call = private/silent". Auto-publishing stranded text would break this documented behavior. Instead, we give the agent a second chance to follow the contract correctly — like returning an undelivered letter and asking the sender to mail it properly, rather than opening and publishing it ourselves.

## Changed files

- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.ts` — followup retry with cleaned transcript fields, room_event gate (+26/-3 net)
- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` — 5 new retry/gate tests replacing 6 bypass tests (-4 net)

## Tests

| Suite | Count | Status |
|-------|-------|--------|
| `agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` | 47 | ✅ All pass |
| `private-message-tool-final.test.ts` | 8 | ✅ All pass |
| `dispatch-from-config.test.ts` | 189 | ✅ All pass (unchanged, confirms no regressions) |
| `followup-runner.test.ts` | 67 | ✅ All pass (confirms followup queue compatibility) |

New test cases:
- `enqueues a followup retry for a stranded substantive reply (#85714)` — verifies `enqueueFollowupRun` is called with retry prompt containing the assistant text
- `does not enqueue retry for short private final replies` — negative case
- `does not enqueue retry when the message tool delivered this turn` — negative case
- `does not enqueue retry for room_event turns (#85714)` — verifies room_event gate
- `clears transcriptPrompt on retry to prevent original prompt from hiding retry instruction (#85714)` — regression test verifying `transcriptPrompt`, `userTurnTranscriptRecorder`, and `currentInboundContext` are all `undefined` on the retry run

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent's final message silently discarded when LLM forgets to call the message tool in `message_tool_only` mode. The fix enqueues a followup retry turn so the agent can deliver via `message(action=send)`, preserving the privacy contract.
- **Real environment tested**: Local macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0, patched checkout at `9dc3c76dc3`.
- **Privacy contract preserved**: The fix does NOT use `deliverDespiteSourceReplySuppression` or `skipSuppressionCheck`. No payload is auto-delivered. The agent is re-prompted to call `message(action=send)` itself.
- **Transcript isolation**: The retry run clears `transcriptPrompt`, `userTurnTranscriptRecorder`, and `currentInboundContext` so the followup runner's `transcriptPrompt ?? extracted.text` resolution correctly uses the retry prompt, not the original user message.
- **Room event safety**: Stranded reply detection is gated by `sessionCtx.InboundEventKind !== "room_event"`, so ambient room events (where silence is intentional) never trigger recovery. Covered by dedicated test case.
- **Failing proof before fix**: On `upstream/main`, `warnPrivateMessageToolFinal` only logs — no retry is enqueued and the reply is silently lost.
- **Evidence after fix**:
  ```
  ✓ auto-reply agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts (47 tests) 1729ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  47 passed (47)

  ✓ unit-fast private-message-tool-final.test.ts (8 tests) 2ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  8 passed (8)

  ✓ auto-reply dispatch-from-config.test.ts (189 tests) 3770ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  189 passed (189)

  ✓ auto-reply followup-runner.test.ts (67 tests) 1710ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  67 passed (67)
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: When a stranded reply is detected, `enqueueFollowupRun` is called with a retry prompt containing the original assistant text and instructions to call `message(action=send)`. The retry run has `transcriptPrompt: undefined` so the followup runner correctly uses the retry instruction. Short replies, already-delivered replies, room events, and runs with existing transcript prompts are all verified by dedicated test cases.
- **What was not tested**: Live end-to-end delivery through an actual channel — the test verifies that the correct followup run is enqueued with the expected prompt shape and cleaned fields. The followup queue machinery (`enqueueFollowupRun` → `scheduleFollowupDrain` → `runReplyAgent`) is a well-tested existing mechanism used for concurrent message queuing.

## Real behavior proof (end-to-end, qa-lab host runner)

This adds a deterministic end-to-end proof that drives the real runtime loop — `runReplyAgent → stranded-final detection → warnPrivateMessageToolFinal → enqueueFollowupRun("stranded-reply-retry") → followup-runner → runEmbeddedAgent → message(action=send) → qa-channel outbound` — not the unit mocks (which stub `enqueueFollowupRun`/`runEmbeddedAgent`).

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Under `messages.visibleReplies=message_tool` (resolved `message_tool_only`), a substantive final reply that never calls the message tool was kept private and silently lost. The fix detects the stranded final and enqueues exactly one bounded followup retry that re-prompts the agent to deliver via `message(action=send)`, preserving the privacy contract; if the retry strands again, no second retry is enqueued.
- **Real environment tested**: macOS Darwin 24.3.0 arm64, Node.js v24.10.0, branch `fix/stranded-reply-pending-delivery-85714` at current HEAD `0469009210` (rebased on latest upstream/main; recovery default-off + collect-batching isolation + updated scenario). qa-lab host runner: in-process gateway child + qa-channel bus + scenario-aware `mock-openai` provider (deterministic by construction; no live model, no Docker).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: ran the new scenario, PASS:
  ```
  node scripts/run-node.mjs qa suite \
    --provider-mode mock-openai \
    --scenario message-tool-stranded-final-recovery \
    --concurrency 1 --fast
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: captured scenario result and the gateway's own runtime log line (ids redacted):
  ```
  COUNTS: { total: 1, passed: 1, failed: 0 }
  step: pass - recovered=1; stranded turns=1; retry delivery turns=1; WARN logged=true

  2026-06-06T06:31:23.411+08:00 [source-reply/private-final] agent produced a long private final reply without calling the configured delivery tool (message_tool_only); response kept private and not delivered to the source channel
  ```
  Asserted from the live request/outbound capture:
  - Turn 1 request: `plannedToolName !== "message"` (long plain-text final, stranded).
  - Exactly one retry request plans the message tool, detected via the verbatim retry needle `you did not call message(action=send)`.
  - Retry delivery request: `plannedToolName === "message"`, `plannedToolArgs.action === "send"`, `plannedToolArgs.message === "QA-STRANDED-85714"`; one outbound on the direct conversation carried the marker (`recovered=1`).
  - After an 8s settle: outbound with the marker stays exactly 1 and message-tool retry deliveries stay exactly 1 (no loop).
- **Observed result after fix**: the stranded `message_tool_only` final was detected and warned, exactly one retry was enqueued, the retry delivered the original text via `message(action=send)` to the channel, and no second retry/delivery occurred — all four invariants observed against the real delivery path.
- **What was not tested**: not run against a live frontier model (deterministic mock by design, since a real model "forgetting" the tool is non-deterministic), and not on a real chat transport (Telegram/WhatsApp/Discord) — exercised on the in-process qa-channel bus; the `message(action=send)` → source-conversation outbound contract is transport-agnostic core auto-reply behavior.

Proof scaffolding added (business logic under `src/auto-reply/` untouched): `qa/scenarios/channels/message-tool-stranded-final-recovery.md` (new scenario) and `extensions/qa-lab/src/providers/mock-openai/server.ts` (two additive deterministic decision branches following the existing `qa group visible reply tool check` pattern).

Closes #85714







## Update — retry drain scheduling (follow-up)

Refined the stranded-reply retry enqueue so it no longer restarts the followup drain while the active reply operation still owns the lane. The retry now enqueues with `restartIfIdle=false` and routes the drain through `scheduleFollowupDrainAfterReplyOperationClear` (the same owner-clear path the normal followup enqueue uses), so the retry only runs once the owning operation releases the lane — removing a potential race with the owner-clear handoff.

- **Changed**: `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.ts` — stranded retry enqueue mirrors the normal enqueue-followup path (dormant enqueue + deferred drain).
- **Test**: `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` — added `schedules the stranded-reply retry drain only after the active reply operation clears`, asserting the drain stays dormant while the reply operation owns the lane and fires only after it clears.

target.title: fix(memory-lancedb): add retry mechanism for Windows Docker bind mount sync delays
target.body:
Hey! 👋

This PR hardens the memory-lancedb plugin initialization path for transient LanceDB table metadata errors seen with Docker bind-mounted data directories.

## The Problem

When a LanceDB data directory is backed by a host bind mount, table metadata can be briefly unavailable after table creation. The previous one-shot initialization path could fail during startup, and the first retry version still had two gaps:

- a table created before `__schema__` cleanup could be reopened and used before cleanup was retried
- the bind-mount guidance was gated on `process.platform === "win32"`, which misses Linux containers running on Docker Desktop

## The Solution

The retry loop now keeps the table local until cleanup succeeds, retries cleanup when a table is reopened, and surfaces generic Docker bind-mount guidance after retry exhaustion.

## What Changed

- Updated `extensions/memory-lancedb/index.ts` to only cache the table after `__schema__` cleanup succeeds.
- Added Docker bind-mount guidance on retry exhaustion regardless of host/runtime platform.
- Added focused coverage in `extensions/memory-lancedb/index.test.ts` for transient create-cleanup failure and exhausted retry diagnostics.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** memory-lancedb can initialize a LanceDB-backed memory table, store a memory, and recall it after this initialization retry hardening.

**Real environment tested:** local OpenClaw plugin registration path using the actual memory-lancedb plugin, actual `@lancedb/lancedb` storage in a temporary database, and a local OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```console
$ NODE_OPTIONS=--no-deprecation node --import tsx /tmp/openclaw-memory-lancedb-real-smoke.ts
```

**Evidence after fix:** copied live console output from the real smoke run:

```console
OpenClaw memory-lancedb real setup smoke
dbPath: <temp>/lancedb
registered tools: memory_forget, memory_recall, memory_store
embedding requests: 2
store action: created
stored id format: uuid
recall count: 1
recalled category: preference
recalled text: I prefer deterministic OpenClaw memory proof runs.
startup log: info:memory-lancedb: plugin registered (db: <temp>/lancedb, lazy init)
```

**Observed result after fix:** `memory_store` created a UUID-backed memory in the LanceDB table, and `memory_recall` returned one recalled preference from that same temporary LanceDB database.

**What was not tested:** I did not run a Windows Docker Desktop bind-mount reproduction locally. The real smoke covers the actual plugin + LanceDB store/recall path; the focused regression tests cover transient cleanup retry and the exhausted-retry Docker bind-mount diagnostic.

## Testing

```console
$ pnpm test extensions/memory-lancedb/index.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 12.34s
```

```console
All matched files use the correct format.
```

```console
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/memory-lancedb/index.ts extensions/memory-lancedb/index.test.ts
```

target.title: feat: block broad protected-root shell searches
target.body:
Closes #99466
Related: #99551
Supersedes: #99581

Supersedes closed PR #99581. GitHub refused to reopen #99581 after the head branch had been force-pushed while closed, so this PR carries the same issue scope plus the latest review fixes.


## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Codex/OpenClaw workers could run broad recursive shell searches over high-risk roots such as a home directory, Codex/OpenClaw state, session archives, repo parents, or external workspace roots. On small PR tasks this can turn command output and local session/debug surfaces into oversized live context, making runaway token usage much more likely.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a high-confidence exec guard for `rg`, recursive `grep`, and `find` commands in gateway/sandbox execution. The guard reuses OpenClaw's existing command-payload analysis so shell wrappers and command carriers are inspected, blocks only protected-root search shapes, and returns actionable guidance to narrow the path, prefer indexed/search tools, and cap output.

This first pass does not add a user-configurable bypass. It is intentionally scoped to the riskiest broad search shapes from the worker-runaway retro and keeps narrowed repo/task/evidence-path searches allowed.

## User Impact

Agents get an immediate, actionable exec failure instead of walking large protected roots. Narrow searches inside a repo or task directory continue to work, and the exec tool description now teaches the safer default before the command is attempted.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/exec-control-command-guard.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec.path.test.ts`
  - `src/infra/exec-control-command-guard.test.ts`: 8 passed
  - `src/agents/bash-tools.exec.path.test.ts`: 43 passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts`
  - 53 passed
- `git diff --check`

Public issue/PR artifacts intentionally avoid raw private transcripts, cookies, endpoint secrets, and full local session logs.

target.body:
## Summary

Add a noop error handler to the ChildProcess returned by `spawnLspServerProcess`. Without it, a missing LSP server binary (ENOENT) emits an async error event that crashes the process.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

**Behavior addressed**: `spawnLspServerProcess` returns a bare ChildProcess without `child.on("error", ...)`. If the LSP binary is missing or cannot start, Node emits an unhandled error event on the child process, crashing the gateway.

**Real environment tested**: Linux, Node 22, OpenClaw main

**Exact steps run after this patch**:
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts
```

**Evidence after fix**:
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
```

New test "suppresses spawn errors on LSP child process": calls `spawnLspServerProcess` with mock spawn, emits `error` on the returned child, and asserts `.not.toThrow()`. This test FAILS on current main because `result.emit("error", ...)` throws `ERR_UNHANDLED_ERROR` when no error listener is registered.

**Before-fix evidence**: `spawnLspServerProcess` returns `spawn(...)` directly — no error handler. `child.emit("error", err)` → `ERR_UNHANDLED_ERROR` → process crash.

**Observed result after fix**: `child.on("error", () => {})` installed before return. Error events on the child process are suppressed. Matches the pattern in supervisor child adapter (#99802) and MCP stdio transport (#99803).

**What was not tested**: Live LSP server binary missing on disk (requires OS-level binary removal).

## Risk

Low. One-line noop handler addition. Same pattern already merged in #99802 and #99803.

target.title: fix(android): propagate CancellationException in CameraHandler catch blocks
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `catch (err: Throwable)` blocks in `CameraHandler.kt`'s three suspend methods (`handleList`, `handleSnap`, `handleClip`) swallow `kotlinx.coroutines.CancellationException`, breaking structured concurrency by silently consuming coroutine cancellation signals. Additionally, `GatewaySession.handleInvokeEvent` catches `Throwable` around `onInvoke` and converts any rethrown `CancellationException` into `InvokeResult.error`, so even after `CameraHandler` rethrows cancellation, it still gets serialized as a normal invoke error at the gateway boundary.

`handleClip` is the worst case — `CameraCaptureManager.clip()` internally hits 6 cancellation points (`delay`, `withTimeout`, `withContext`). When the scope is cancelled (e.g., talk mode moves to background), `CancellationException` is caught and returned as a normal `InvokeResult.error`, so the parent coroutine never learns that cancellation occurred.

The codebase already has the correct pattern in `GatewaySession.kt:441-443` and `TalkModeManager.kt:897-899`, where `CancellationException` is re-thrown before the generic `Throwable` catch. `CameraHandler` and the invoke boundary missed this.

## Why This Change Was Made

1. **`CameraHandler.kt`**: Added `catch (err: CancellationException) { throw err }` before each of the 5 `catch (err: Throwable)` blocks in `handleList`, `handleSnap`, and `handleClip`, preserving structured concurrency semantics. No other logic changed — the existing error-handling paths remain identical for all non-cancellation exceptions.

2. **`GatewaySession.kt`**: Added the same `catch (err: CancellationException) { throw err }` before `catch (err: Throwable)` in `handleInvokeEvent` at the production invoke boundary (line 1018). This prevents the rethrown cancellation from being serialized as `InvokeResult.error`, following the same pattern already used at `GatewaySession.kt:441`.

## User Impact

- Coroutine cancellation during camera operations (`handleList`, `handleSnap`, `handleClip`) is now correctly propagated at both the handler and invoke-boundary layers
- `handleClip`'s `finally` block (restoring `externalAudioCaptureActive`) still runs correctly on cancellation
- Complements the talk mode background audio fix (7481712f8e) for correct background resource cleanup

## Evidence

- CameraHandler tests: 6/6 passed ✅
- Pattern consistency with existing `GatewaySession.kt:441-443`
- CI: all checks green (android-build-play, android-test-play, android-test-third-party, plus all core checks)

### Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: CancellationException propagation during camera coroutine operations (handleList/handleSnap/handleClip) through both CameraHandler and GatewaySession invoke boundary.

Real environment tested: Linux x86_64 (NewStartOS V4.4.2, kernel 4.19.112-2.el8), JDK 21.0.11 (Temurin), Gradle 9.5.1, Android SDK 36, branch `fix/android-camerahandler-cancellation-leak`, commits `79ea25420e`.

Changes: +11 lines in CameraHandler.kt (5 CancellationException rethrow blocks), +2 lines in GatewaySession.kt (1 CancellationException rethrow at invoke boundary).

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```
source ~/android-env.sh
./gradlew :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests "ai.openclaw.app.node.CameraHandlerTest"
```

Evidence after fix:

```
> Task :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest
BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 8s
31 actionable tasks: 5 executed, 26 up-to-date
```

All 6 CameraHandlerTest cases passed with zero failures. The CancellationException rethrow blocks compile and pass existing tests — no regression.

Observed result after fix: Existing CameraHandler tests continue to pass. The catch blocks correctly allow CancellationException to propagate while still handling all other Throwable types as before. The fix is purely additive — no existing behavior path is altered. The GatewaySession change mirrors the existing pattern at line 441.

What was not tested: Real-device Android testing with actual camera hardware (requires physical device with CameraX). The fix is structural (additive catch clause before existing handler), so the risk of device-specific regression is negligible. The `handleClip` `finally` block (`externalAudioCaptureActive.value = false`) is structurally unchanged and runs on both normal return and cancellation paths.
